producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 148 BPM, 4/4, D-flat major. Fast, bright and relentless. It starts at full speed and never eases off.

VOICE: Male tenor, urgent and slightly strained, as if singing while running. Verses are tumbling and breathless with no gaps between lines. The chorus is held high and pushed. Doubled in the chorus. No harmonies until the outro.

INSTRUMENTS: A chiming electric guitar playing a rapid, climbing single-note riff that never stops. A second guitar on big ringing chords. Bass playing driving eighth notes. A glossy synth pad and a string-like synth line in the chorus. Tight, fast drums with busy hi-hats and a snare on every backbeat.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, the guitar riff alone, bass joins after two bars. 0:13 Verse 1, drums in. 0:39 Pre-chorus in half time. 0:52 Chorus 1. 1:18 Riff, 4 bars. 1:24 Verse 2, the same words, sung harder. 1:50 Pre-chorus. 2:03 Chorus 2. 2:29 Instrumental, the riff with the synth line. 2:42 Chorus repeated. 3:08 Outro, the last phrase six times over the full band, then a dead stop at 3:35.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Early-2000s indie rock with new-wave gloss: bright, dense and slightly over-compressed, guitars wide, synths shining over the top.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The guitar riff in the first two seconds, before anything else enters.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The trigger is a notification, the scene is a kitchen, and the narrator has a cat to feed. The spiral is the same at forty as it was at twenty, and the outro says the quiet part out loud six times.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Forced calm, spiral, denial, and denial again.
